The event calendar and ongoing risks look much different over the next four weeks than they did going into the previous four weeks. This move is getting long in the tooth and I think it's more likely than not that Waller's speech + today's CPI has provided an attractive opportunity to flip from a short to a long risk bias into next week's Anthropic IPO and possibly longer, TBD. This is not an all clear of the structural problems that exist, but a local call that the path to the final destination will not be easy nor in a straight line.

Kinetiq is building the app economy around Hyperliquid.

Elysium is Kinetiq’s new network for the apps that run alongside Hyperliquid’s exchange, targeting roughly 100 times the block space they get on HyperEVM today. 

Block space has been a key bottleneck on HyperEVM. Market makers pay gas on every quote update, so fee spikes mean fewer updates and wider spreads. Few apps beyond staking and lending have taken off.

More room should let market makers keep prices fresh without fees eating into their margins. A maker selling downside protection through an options app on Elysium could then hedge with perps on Hyperliquid. Each of those trades pays the exchange a fee.

HIP-3 let outside teams launch their own markets on Hyperliquid. Elysium could do the same for apps.

$WGS earnings. Market cap roughly $1.6B. The good: revenue $123M, margins improved to 72%, adjusted profit $8.6M, reimbursements up 5%, genome collection rates improving, and Medicaid coverage expanding. The bad: volume growth slowing, guidance lowered, reimbursement documentation creating delays, and Medicare reimbursement cuts presenting a 2027 headwind. What needs to happen for the stock to recover? The company needs to reaccelerate volume growth, improve reimbursement collection, reduce payment delays, and demonstrate that expanding Medicaid coverage can translate into sustainable revenue and earnings growth. The entire genomics sector has been under pressure, with even $ILMN down roughly 30%. I believe $WGS will start running again when the sector recovers. I’m not increasing my exposure today because I already have enough, but I’m not selling either. If I had less exposure, I would probably be buying more. 

When $WGS reached $100, it got there without any logic. 
There was no meaningful improvement in the underlying business, yet the stock price had doubled. Now it’s being oversold again because of market sentiment and pressure across the entire sector. This is simply the nature of stock market cycles. Prices can become completely disconnected from business fundamentals in both directions. You buy when pessimism becomes excessive and sell when optimism exceeds logic.

When diversification is mentioned in investing - many take the idea that its only because of being wrong on a single investment

However just as important is diversification on time horizons

As per BTC last 5 years, gold before that, SP across a decade before that - there are periods where any asset is flat or down across a long period of time - you could be right long term but that doesnt mean you get to pick when the returns come

Having focused diversification is how you can smooth liquidity and returns over time

Why do very rich who know SP does better than alot of  funds long term still invest in special funds? Its not because they are stupid - they want liquidity and returns to happen in years their other assets dont do well so that they have liquidity in good and bad times

SP is not immune to downside risk - people have just forgotten that it can happen as it did in 90s-2000s for over a decade

As opposite eg if last 10yrs or 5rs you had many ups and downs in BTC, gold, SP but if you owned all 3 you would have been liquid and up and to the right smoothing out volatility in any one single asset

You dont need to own 10-20 things but you should own in my humble opinion at least 3 different asset classes and then have long time frames of 5-10yrs at min

Dont invest with money you need short term
